products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a non-profit government laboratory. Its website describes it as recruiting global talent in artificial intelligence, large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, foundational platforms, and related fields, with the stated goal of creating a better AGI future. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, including Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University. The site also advertises a 2026 global campus recruitment and a "Polaris" talent plan.

The site lists several releases. At the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum, the lab announced an upgraded Shusheng Duanyan scientific discovery platform and opened its full-stack services, described as combining calculation, proof, and verification. It also released the Shusheng physical world model W0 and the Shusheng embodied full-stack engine Intern-Robotics, which the site says addresses data, training, and application for embodied intelligence. Professor Zhou Bowen is quoted proposing that scientific research is the next programming and that AI and science form a dual-wheel drive. At the 2026 WAIC science frontier forum, the lab and partners released ten joint innovation results in life sciences, materials science, and deep space astronomy.

The lab's site also describes an AI safety framework called the AI-45-degree balance law, with a causal path through general alignment, intervenability, and reflection, and a risk management process covering assessment, training, base models, applications, and verification. InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab) is listed as a Chinese open-source LLM, with academic research and cross-border data review advised.
